featured_reviews.name: Riya Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the Worst Gym Experiences – Not Worth Your Time or Money

I rarely leave negative reviews, but after months of giving Flex Gym the benefit of the doubt, I feel compelled to share my experience so others don’t waste their time like I did.

First of all, the facility maintenance is pathetic. There’s been a persistent water leakage issue in multiple areas of the gym, especially around the ceiling and changing rooms. It’s not only inconvenient but straight-up dangerous—I've seen people slip, and the staff just casually mop it up without addressing the root problem. The smell of dampness in certain corners is unbearable, and it’s clear management has no intention of fixing it any time soon.

Secondly, the gym is overcrowded at nearly all hours, making it impossible to get a proper workout in. Whether you go in the morning, afternoon, or evening, you’ll find long queues for basic equipment, weights scattered everywhere, and zero enforcement of discipline on the floor. Members do whatever they want—hogging equipment, dropping weights, playing loud music—and no one steps in to manage the chaos.

The trainers are hardly any help either. Most of them are either busy chatting with their friends or paying attention only to their personal training clients. One staff member, Shweta, in particular, has been repeatedly rude and unapproachable. Instead of helping members or maintaining order, she seems more interested in power-tripping or gossiping at the front desk.

To make matters worse, the owner Brajesh Gupta is completely uninvolved. He clearly doesn’t care about the gym’s condition or member experience—there’s no quality control, no feedback mechanism, and no visible effort to improve anything. It honestly feels like they’re just there to collect fees without offering any value in return.

There’s no cap on memberships, so the place is packed beyond capacity every day. Even during "off-peak" hours, there’s barely enough space to move, let alone train effectively.

Save yourself the frustration. There are far better gyms out there that actually invest in their infrastructure, enforce discipline, and treat members with respect. Until Flex Gym sorts out its serious hygiene, management, and behavioral issues, I’d strongly recommend staying away.

featured_reviews.name: Nishi Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
My experience with WOD Mumbai was extremely disappointing and a complete breach of trust.

The owner, Brian, personally assured me that he would train me and that I would receive 15 sessions per month instead of the standard 12. Based on his verbal commitment, we agreed on ₹90,000 for 3 months, amounting to 45 sessions. I paid the full amount in cash, trusting his word.

After completing 34 sessions, he suddenly denied ever making this promise and backed out entirely. When confronted, he asked if I had anything in writing—despite the agreement being based solely on his assurance. This was both shocking and disheartening.

There were also clear professionalism issues. My new mat went missing due to staff/gym mismanagement, and I was asked to use a used mat, which I refused. Instead of handling the situation professionally, it was made uncomfortable, even though the fault was clearly not mine.

Despite multiple promises, no diet plan or real guidance was ever provided. The training felt purely transactional—focused on counting hours rather than offering genuine coaching or support.

Initially, everything was presented very convincingly, but in reality, promises were not honored. Based on my experience, I strongly advise anyone considering this gym to get every commitment in writing. Trust alone is clearly not enough here.
